This study investigates the discretization of a distributed control problem involving random evolution equations within a spatially discrete framework. We establish the existence of an optimal solution for the discrete problem and subsequently establish its convergence to the optimal solution of the continuous, stochastic problem.

The Pierre Auger Observatory has detected a directional preference in cosmic rays exceeding 4 EeV, with a statistical significance surpassing 4.5 sigma. This anisotropy is most prominent in the 4–8 EeV range, where it exhibits a 100-degree rotational symmetry and a 1.5 sigma significance. The findings are consistent with a 100-degree symmetric pattern observed in the 8–16 EeV range, which shares a similar significance level. These results are interpreted as evidence for a cosmic-ray source distribution located at a distance of approximately 100 Mpc, characterized by a 100-degree symmetry.

This paper establishes that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra defined over a field with positive characteristic zero must be solvable. This finding serves as a non-abelian generalization of both the Havlicek and Dzhumadil'daev results, which previously demonstrated the solvability of Nijenhuis-Schroder and pre-Lie algebra structures under similar conditions.

The findings reveal that the second-order event plane angle exhibits a correlation with the second-order flow coefficient ($v_2$) that increases with collision centrality. This study introduces a novel approach to resolving inconsistencies in tabular data containing missing values, grounded in the concept of functional dependencies. We define a specific class of relations that incorporates nulls and establish a formal framework for representing tables populated with such relations. Within this setting, we define and examine the "chase" operation, which serves to identify and resolve discrepancies. Furthermore, we present a polynomial-time algorithm designed to detect whether a given relation is satisfiable.

This study introduces the TV-PAR model, a novel framework designed for analyzing and forecasting Poisson-distributed time series data that exhibit both seasonal patterns and trends evolving over time. The model integrates a seasonal autoregressive component with a new temporal variation mechanism specifically tailored for Poisson series. We evaluate the TV-PAR model's performance through extensive simulations and by applying it to real-world datasets, demonstrating its efficacy in various practical scenarios.

Neural representations have emerged as a leading approach for modeling high-resolution, complex 3D objects. However, current methods often lack the ability to generalize across different views and handle missing data, largely because they fail to account for the underlying symmetries inherent in 3D geometry. To address this, we introduce Neural Description Fields (NeuroDesc), a novel framework that integrates SE(3)-equivariance into neural object representations. NeuroDesc employs a hierarchical architecture: a view-dependent decoder generates local descriptions of object patches, while a global descriptor predicts the transformation required to align these patches into a canonical view. By leveraging SE(3)-symmetry, this design enables the system to synthesize novel images from unseen perspectives and robustly reconstruct objects even when input data contains occlusions or gaps. We validate our approach through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its efficacy in high-fidelity rendering and robust reconstruction.

We establish the global positioning of the Yang-Lee edge singularity (YLES) within the extensive taxonomy of universality classes defined by continuous symmetries. By applying the $\epsilon$-expansion method to compute critical exponents for the 2D Ising model at complex magnetic fields, we identify the precise universality category of the YLES across various spatial dimensions. Our analysis reveals that the YLES belongs to the same universality class as the standard 2D Ising transition at zero magnetic field, suggesting it functions as a genuine 2D Ising critical point. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the YLES shares its universality class with the standard 2D Ising model in all other dimensions $d \geq 2$.

This work presents a new proof of the local convexity of the TAP free energy, a property previously established by Ben Arous and Guionnet using the stochastic calculus of complex-valued Brownian motion. This result is crucial for analyzing the uniqueness of solutions to the TAP equations and characterizing the thermodynamic behavior of spin systems. The proof relies on the Sudakov-Fernique inequality, specifically its application to approximate message passing (AMP) iterations known as "S-AMP." The authors introduce a novel proof demonstrating that S-AMP satisfies the Gaussian comparison lemma, which serves as the foundation for the local convexity argument. Furthermore, the authors leverage this Gaussian comparison proof to establish the Sudakov-Fernique inequality for a broader class of iterated AMP schemes, termed "post-AMP." This extended framework encompasses various message passing algorithms, including belief propagation, and the proof of the Gaussian comparison lemma for these schemes constitutes the core of the paper's contribution.

This study introduces a novel technique for estimating aerosol optical depth (AOD) using stellar photometry data collected by ground-based telescopes. The method relies on the premise that stellar flux attenuation caused by atmospheric aerosols adheres to the same physical laws governing solar irradiance attenuation. By applying the single-scattering albedo model to stellar observations, we derived a straightforward formula linking AOD to the magnitude difference between an affected star and its clear-sky counterpart. We validated this approach using the ZTF (Zwicky Transient Facility) dataset, which yielded results consistent with independent AOD measurements from the NASA MODIS satellite. Furthermore, we developed a machine learning algorithm to enhance the precision of these estimates. Leveraging the vast volume of stellar photometry available from ZTF, this framework offers a powerful means to monitor global aerosol loading with high temporal resolution.

This study introduces DeepHMap++, a novel pose estimation framework designed to accurately determine the full degrees of freedom (DoF) poses of objects within images. The proposed method integrates two primary components: a correspondence learning module and a projection clustering module. The correspondence learning module utilizes a deep neural network to predict initial 2D-3D feature matches, which are subsequently refined through a correspondence optimization algorithm to ensure high precision. Complementing this, the projection clustering module employs a hierarchical clustering strategy to identify clusters of 3D points that project onto the same 2D locations, thereby enabling the robust estimation of full DoF poses even under conditions of partial occlusion. Extensive experiments conducted on the LINEMOD and YCB-Video datasets demonstrate that DeepHMap++ achieves state-of-the-art performance in both accuracy and robustness.

GGLasso is a Python library designed to facilitate the estimation of graphical models through the maximization of Gaussian graphical Lasso objectives. It offers a user-friendly interface for solving generalized graph lasso problems, which involve optimizing quadratic forms subject to sparse inverse Wishart priors. This capability allows users to estimate sparse precision matrices across multiple related datasets simultaneously. Furthermore, GGLasso supports the estimation of graph-structured sparsity by incorporating constraints on the adjacency matrices of various graphs within the solution. The library includes specialized algorithms tailored for these generalized graph lasso scenarios and provides tools for post-estimation analysis, such as visualizing the resulting network structures.

Molecular dynamics simulations are a fundamental tool for investigating the physical and chemical characteristics of biomolecules and other molecular systems. However, these simulations frequently encounter difficulties in accurately sampling configurational space, particularly when systems exhibit multiple metastable states separated by substantial free energy barriers. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel, efficient configurational sampling technique grounded in Langevin dynamics. This approach integrates a recently developed, robust, and adaptable method for integrating stochastic differential equations, which ensures the preservation of time-reversibility and ensures the preservation of the correct invariant distribution. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through applications to the study of protein folding and the self-assembly of micelles, highlighting its practical utility in complex scenarios.

This study introduces Eigenvector Prominance (EVP), a novel method designed to identify and evaluate the importance of individual layers within multilayer networks. The approach relies on the concept of Eigenvector Centrality (EVC) to assess the significance of each network layer. The core premise of EVP is that a layer is more critical if it contains highly connected nodes that are also well-connected within other layers. The proposed framework is applied to analyze the structure of multilayer networks, specifically focusing on the organization of the brain.

This work presents the derivation of Dirac's formula within R-matrix spacetimes, a framework where the Minkowski metric is expressed as a product of two complex matrices. This approach offers a novel perspective on the geometry of spacetime, enabling the construction of a Dirac spinor field theory that aligns with the established classical and quantum models.

This study investigates the liquid entry surface seal (LESS) phenomenon occurring when a sphere, moving at moderate speeds, contacts a liquid surface. The research focuses on the sphere's trajectory immediately following contact, specifically examining the transition from the initial acceleration phase to the subsequent deceleration phase. To achieve this, a theoretical framework was developed that integrates a force balance equation with a model describing the seal's growth rate. This approach allows for the prediction of the transition velocity based on key parameters, including sphere diameter, impact speed, liquid surface tension, and viscosity. The theoretical predictions were rigorously validated against experimental data gathered across a range of conditions. Furthermore, the research offers a novel methodology for determining the seal growth rate, which was applied to analyze the influence of varying sphere diameters and speeds on the growth dynamics.

We examine the structure of Type IIB effective field theories (EFTs) to determine the form of the theta-term and its generalization, and we establish that the most extended version of this term is always a total derivative. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a non-vanishing expectation value for the axion field invariably leads to a reduction in the symmetry of the EFT. We also explore the implications of a non-zero vacuum expectation value for the theta parameter, showing that it generates mass for some scalars and fermions while leaving the remaining symmetries intact. Finally, we argue that a non-vanishing expectation value for the theta parameter is a universal feature of these EFTs, regardless of the specific matter content or the details of compactification.

The electronic structure of transition metal sulfides and their sulfosalts is frequently shaped by strong electron correlations, which can drive orbital-selective phenomena such as symmetry breaking and metal-insulator transitions. This study investigates the cubic chalcocopper sulfide mineral cubanite ($\text{CuFe}_2\text{S}_3$), a material known for its high electrical conductivity and lack of magnetic order. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the ground state of cubanite exhibits a symmetry-lifted configuration where the $t_{2g}$ $d$-orbitals of Fe split into a lower-energy $d_{xy}$ orbital and an upper-energy pair ($d_{xz}, d_{yz}$). This arrangement results in a non-degenerate, symmetry-broken insulating state with a band gap of approximately 0.5 eV, which aligns well with experimental observations. The formation of this gap is attributed to a Jahn-Teller-like effect, where the lattice relaxes to lower the energy of the occupied $d_{xy}$ band while pushing the empty $d_{xz}, d_{yz}$ bands higher. The resulting electronic configuration is identified as $(d_{xy})^6(d_{xz}, d_{yz})^4$, corresponding to a $S=1$ state. This study examines the effects of an electric field on a semiconductor quantum dot containing a dark exciton with an additional trapped impurity ion. The analysis derives the system's energy levels and wave functions within the parabolic potential approximation. Furthermore, it investigates the temporal evolution of the dark exciton's Rabi oscillations under varying conditions of impurity ion strength and electric field intensity.

This study investigates the electronic band structures of a two-dimensional non-symmorphic wallpaper lattice featuring a two-atom basis, specifically within the P2mg space group. We demonstrate that introducing a tunable mass term into a Dirac cone located at the high-symmetry M point causes the Dirac cone to split into two distinct Dirac points. Crucially, the positions of these points can be adjusted by varying the mass parameter, allowing them to be driven either apart or back together. Furthermore, we explore the topological characteristics of this system, revealing that it hosts a non-trivial Chern number and exhibits a tunable quantum anomalous Hall effect.

Single-photon quantum optical catalysis represents a novel non-linear mechanism capable of generating complex multi-photon states from simple initial inputs. This paper investigates the creation of single-photon facilitated coherent states (SPFCS) by passing a coherent state through a single-photon catalyzed beam splitter. We demonstrate that these states exhibit non-classical properties, including negative Wigner functions, strong squeezing, and photon number entanglement between the input and output ports. Furthermore, we establish that SPFCS functions as a resource for quantum-enhanced phase estimation, surpassing the standard quantum limit. Finally, we explore the generation of single-photon assisted Schrödinger cat states via the interference of two such beams on a beam splitter.

This work examines bivectors within the General Relativity framework using Newman-Penrose methods. It details the construction of self-dual and anti-self-dual bivectors from the NP tetrad, demonstrating that any bivector can be expressed as a linear combination of these components. The text further analyzes the geometric meaning of these objects, illustrating how the NP tetrad can be derived from a bivector. Finally, it applies this formalism to Maxwell's equations and the gravitational field equations, showing that in both cases, the field strength and Weyl tensors decompose into self-dual and anti-self-dual parts.

This study introduces a novel method for inferring monomer compositions within polymer sequences using linear regression and integer programming. The proposed approach is evaluated against existing techniques on both synthetic data and real-world biological sequences, demonstrating superior performance in handling noisy datasets and emerging as a promising tool for analyzing polymers in biological contexts.

Accurate segmentation of esophageal neoplasms is crucial for effective treatment planning, yet it remains challenging due to the organ's complex shape, the disease's heterogeneous nature, and the lack of distinct anatomical boundaries in CT scans. To address these issues, we propose DDAUnet, a novel framework built upon a Dense Unet architecture enhanced with dilated convolutional blocks. This design aims to improve segmentation precision by capturing multi-scale features and focusing on critical regions. Specifically, DDAUnet employs a dual attention mechanism that integrates both channel and spatial dimensions to refine feature maps. Furthermore, the model incorporates a dynamic loss function designed to mitigate class imbalance caused by the small size of neoplasm regions relative to the entire scan. Evaluated on a private dataset of 100 CT scans containing neoplastic esophageal lesions, DDAUnet achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.811 and a Hausdorff Distance (HD) of 10.33. These results indicate that DDAUnet offers superior performance compared to existing methods, making it a promising solution for the automated segmentation of esophageal neoplasms.

The rise of the internet has enabled multilingual individuals to communicate across language barriers, leading to a common practice of mixing languages within a single utterance, known as code-switching or code-mixing. While this phenomenon offers significant advantages for multilingual groups, it simultaneously presents substantial challenges for Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. This paper examines the primary obstacles and contributing factors affecting NLP when dealing with code-mixed text. We categorize these elements into three groups: linguistic characteristics, the specific languages involved, and the context of use. Furthermore, we outline several promising research directions aimed at advancing NLP capabilities for code-mixed data.

Automatic image captioning systems are increasingly used to provide textual descriptions for visual content. A primary method for evaluating these systems involves comparing their generated captions against a set of high-quality references, typically created by human annotators. However, this standard approach faces a significant limitation: it treats all references within a specific image's cluster as equally valid, ignoring the reality that human annotations often vary in accuracy. To address this, we introduce a novel framework that leverages human reference data to assess the trustworthiness of individual annotations. By integrating this reliability assessment into the caption evaluation process, we develop a more robust and precise metric. Our proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to existing evaluation metrics across multiple datasets.

Ta$_2$O$_5$ is a promising candidate for next-generation high-k dielectrics, yet its base state crystal structure remains elusive. This study employs a systematic approach combining Monte Carlo simulations and density functional theory (DFT) to evaluate 12 candidate configurations. Our analysis reveals that the P2$_1$/n structure exhibits the lowest formation energy, making it the most energetically favorable candidate. Furthermore, this P2$_1$/n phase demonstrates superior mechanical stability and a high negative formation volume coefficient, suggesting it is likely the true ground state. Consequently, we propose the P2$_1$/n configuration as the base state of Ta$_2$O$_5$.

This study investigates the role of large-scale geographic clustering in spreading misinformation within the Reddit community. We analyze a dataset comprising 1.5 million comments from 1,000 misinformation-related threads across 100 U.S. subreddits, covering the period from January 2018 to December 2019. Our analysis reveals that while misinformation often originates from a single location, it typically spreads to multiple geographically distinct areas. Furthermore, we observe that misinformation comments originating from these large geographic arrangements are significantly more likely to receive upvotes compared to those from single locations. This increased visibility is attributed to the fact that comments from large geographic arrangements attract more replies, thereby generating greater engagement. These findings suggest that the presence of widespread geographic distribution functions as a mechanism for the increased dissemination of misinformation within Reddit.

This study investigates the acoustic patterns within human-instructor-robot interaction scenarios, specifically focusing on tasks requiring physical manipulation. We hypothesize that these vocal patterns serve as a valuable, underutilized data source for enhancing the capabilities of robotic assistants. To test this, we developed a novel dataset capturing the sounds instructors make while guiding robots through manipulation tasks. This collection represents the first dataset of its kind, featuring audio recordings of human collaboration with robots. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of the dataset's acoustic characteristics and explored the relationship between these vocal features and the specific manipulation actions performed. The findings reveal that the dataset exhibits distinct acoustic traits and demonstrate that vocal patterns correlate significantly with the types of manipulation actions executed. These results support the hypothesis that human vocalizations during robot-assisted tasks contain meaningful information regarding physical actions. Consequently, this insight offers a promising avenue for future research into leveraging audio data to improve robotic manipulation performance.

This work examines the Euler-Arnold equations governing rigid body motion, ideal fluid flow on a Lie group, and the dynamics of an elastic rod. It establishes that these systems are geometrically intricate, a characteristic defined by the existence of a non-trivial, compact, simply connected, smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a Riemannian metric $g$ such that the associated skew-symmetric operator $\ad^{\dagger}_g$ fails to be algebraic. The paper further demonstrates that these equations are geometrically simple, meaning the operator $\ad^{\dagger}_g$ is algebraic for all elements on a specific class of compact, smooth, connected manifolds. These findings offer a geometric framework for analyzing the integrability and complexity of Euler-Poincaré reductions.

Conversational agents are increasingly utilized to handle user interactions across a wide range of applications. However, developing these systems often involves subjective and inconsistent evaluation methods, which can lead to unfair assessments. To address this issue, we introduce an automated evaluation framework designed to ensure fairness and consistency. This framework incorporates a standardized dataset, a unified evaluation protocol, and a benchmarking suite. We apply this system to evaluate several prominent chatbots, revealing significant disparities in how different teams assess their own models. Furthermore, we propose a novel metric to quantify the reliability of self-reported evaluations. Our analysis indicates that the consistency of these self-assessments varies substantially depending on the specific application domain.

This study introduces Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation (MSDC-Rec), a novel framework designed to tackle the challenge of sparse user-item interactions prevalent in multi-sparse recommendation domains. By integrating diverse recommendation systems, MSDC-Rec facilitates the sharing of information across domains to enhance individual domain performance. Specifically, the proposed method employs a thorough aspect preference learning mechanism to extract implicit user preferences from sparse data, while simultaneously modeling the correlations between these aspects and those in other domains to enable effective information transfer. Furthermore, the framework incorporates a multi-sparse domain collaborative module that leverages the interplay among various domains to boost overall recommendation quality. Extensive experiments conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate that MSDC-Rec significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in terms of recommendation accuracy.

This study introduces Hypatia. jl, a new open-source package designed for Julia that specializes in handling conic formulations of mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problems. The software enables users to define these problems using Julia's native syntax while automatically generating the corresponding mathematical models and solver-specific code. A key feature of Hypatia. jl is its support for a wide array of convex functions, including those defined by custom user code. The paper illustrates the package's capabilities by applying it to resolve the well-known organic rank minimization problem. Additionally, it presents a new, efficient Julia-based implementation for the specific class of piecewise linear functions known as "hinge functions."

Automated quality assurance (QA) systems are essential for ensuring the reliability of cerebral MRI data analysis pipelines. While deep learning models have demonstrated significant potential in this domain, they often struggle to generalize to unseen datasets, a challenge exacerbated by the inherent heterogeneity of MRI acquisition protocols. This study investigates the generalization capabilities of QA models across multiple dimensions, including variations in scanner hardware, acquisition parameters, and patient demographics. We introduce a novel framework utilizing a diverse collection of publicly available MRI QA datasets to evaluate how these factors influence performance. Our findings reveal that current QA deep learning architectures are highly sensitive to shifts in acquisition parameters and scanner types, yet they remain relatively robust against demographic changes. Furthermore, we observe that the severity of performance degradation due to domain shifts is not uniform; it varies depending on the specific task and the particular data dimension involved. Finally, we propose a new metric designed to quantify the magnitude of domain shifts across different dimensions, offering a more granular assessment of generalization challenges.

The escalating frequency and severity of natural disasters and human-induced incidents have significantly compromised the resilience of power systems. While the integration of electric vehicles (EVs) offers a pathway to a more sustainable future, it simultaneously introduces new challenges regarding power system resilience. This paper introduces a novel multi-agent optimization framework designed to evaluate the impact of privately held EVs on distribution network resilience. The proposed method models the complex interactions among EVs, charging stations, and distribution networks, incorporating the stochastic nature of EV arrival and departure patterns. Furthermore, it addresses the critical issue of post-disaster EV charging by optimizing the placement of mobile charging stations. The study details the construction of a multi-agent model that captures the decision-making processes of EVs, charging stations, and the distribution network, alongside the development of a specific mobile charging station placement strategy. Finally, the framework's efficacy is demonstrated through a case study of a distribution network containing various charging station types and a population of private EVs.

This study introduces a Multi-Agent Recurrent Meeting (MARM) framework designed to enhance the efficiency of multi-agent interactions by facilitating repeated meetings among agents. Unlike existing approaches, MARM does not require pre-defined meeting locations or fixed schedules. Instead, it employs an incentive mechanism based on travel distance to autonomously determine both the venue and the timing of these recurring encounters. The proposed method was rigorously evaluated through extensive simulations and real-world experiments involving various agent types and scenarios. Results indicate that MARM successfully fosters repeated meetings, yielding significant performance improvements for participating agents.

This study employs first-principles calculations to explore the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of XSn$_3$ (X = Gd, Cm) and Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ compounds. The research focuses on the cubic MgAgAs-type structure, utilizing the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) within the framework of density functional theory (DFT) to model these systems. The results indicate that both XSn$_3$ compounds exhibit metallic behavior with ferromagnetic ordering, characterized by a positive magnetic moment on the Sn atoms. The magnetic moments of Gd and Cm atoms are found to be approximately 7.0 $\mu_B$ and 7.2 $\mu_B$, respectively, aligning well with experimental data. The magnetic moments of Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ are observed to be slightly higher than those of pure XSn$_3$ compounds. Furthermore, the study investigates the effects of doping on the electronic and magnetic properties of these materials.

This study examines the production of additional baryons and mesons in the atmosphere, with a specific focus on the impact of high-energy cosmic ray showers. The paper outlines the methodology used to generate predictions for these extra particles, which are then compared against existing experimental data. The analysis reveals that current datasets are insufficient to accurately determine the production rates of these additional baryons and mesons. Furthermore, the research highlights a significant gap in current knowledge regarding the yields of these particles within the upper atmosphere.

This paper offers a new proof of the foundation theorem for the special orthogonal group $SO(n,\mathbb{R})$, utilizing the B-type Coxeter group $B(n)$ and its associated Hecke algebra. This approach generalizes a prior result by the author concerning the special linear group $SL(n,\mathbb{R})$ and its A-type counterpart, $A(n-1)$. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the classical Iwasawa decomposition for $SO(n,\mathbb{R})$ can be generalized to arbitrary complex semisimple Lie groups.

This study presents the first analysis of weak gravitational lensing magnification applied to Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) within the Pantheon dataset. By leveraging the galaxy distribution from the Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey (DECaLS) to generate a convergence map, we examine the relationship between the observed SN positions and the resulting lensing effects. Our findings indicate that the mean magnification across the sample is $0.000 \pm 0.001$, with a standard deviation of $0.001 \pm 0.001$. Furthermore, we observe a correlation between the magnitude of the magnification and the distance to the nearest large-scale structure, suggesting that this phenomenon could be leveraged to enhance the precision of cosmological parameter estimation in future, larger surveys.

Photonic silicon-on-dielectric material (SiPh) is a leading technology for high-speed, energy-efficient optical interconnects within data centers. However, the inherent high refractive index of silicon causes significant optical loss at bends and T-junctions, which restricts the design of compact photonic circuits. This study introduces a novel T-junction architecture for SiPh that achieves a 90-degree turn with a footprint of merely 100×100 μm² while maintaining a 3 dB insertion loss. The design leverages a 90-degree turn mechanism previously developed for 90-degree turns, which has been adapted for T-junctions. The paper details the design methodology, fabrication process, and experimental validation of the T-junction. Results indicate that the fabricated device operates at a wavelength of 1550 nm, exhibits a 3 dB insertion loss, and a 3 dB bandwidth of 100 nm. The study concludes by discussing the implications of this T-junction design for the development of more complex photonic circuits.

Object detection methods have advanced significantly, yet most existing research focuses on optimizing models for individual objects in isolation, overlooking the crucial role of surrounding context. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates contextual information into detection tasks. We present a new dataset featuring 100 distinct objects, each captured in 1,000 images with diverse contextual variations. Furthermore, we establish a standardized benchmark for evaluating object detectors within these complex scenarios. Our analysis reveals that current state-of-the-art detectors perform poorly when objects are embedded in unfamiliar contexts, and we demonstrate that incorporating contextual data substantially enhances detection accuracy.

This study investigates the existence of solutions within a class of inhomogeneous Kirchhoff-type elliptic problems defined on $\mathbb{R}^2$. These problems incorporate both a singular nonlinearity and the Trudinger-Moser power expansion. By applying variational techniques, we establish that multiple solutions exist for this framework. Specifically, we demonstrate the existence of at least one ground state solution and a second solution characterized by high energy.

This paper examines the concentration disparities among binary random variables that are pairwise negatively correlated and share an identical expectation. We establish a new result demonstrating that the ratio between the maximum and minimum variances for such variables is bounded by a function dependent solely on the system size $n$. This bound is shown to be tight for specific cases, including the well-known "star" configuration. Furthermore, we explore the problem within the context of the "complete bipartite graph" configuration, offering a novel proof for the previously documented tight bound associated with this setup.

This paper offers a new proof of a result by F. Knop, demonstrating that any symplectic modification of an affine variety constitutes a symplectic modification of the same degree. Additionally, the authors introduce a concept of "symplectic modification of degree zero" and utilize it to show that any such modification is necessarily birationally trivial.

Kidney transplant success relies heavily on minimizing the HLA mismatch between donor and recipient, yet the scarcity of compatible organs has led to the widespread acceptance of incompatible kidneys. This study investigates the optimal allocation of these incompatible kidneys, specifically examining the optimal acceptance criteria for such donations. We demonstrate that the ideal strategy involves accepting incompatible kidneys only when the resulting post-transplant utility surpasses that of remaining on the waiting list. Furthermore, we derive a closed-form expression for the optimal acceptance threshold and provide numerical simulations to illustrate how this threshold varies with the specific characteristics of the transplant program.

Word embeddings are increasingly utilized in financial research, yet their ability to accurately reflect the sentiment polarity of words remains under-investigated. This study examines the semantic and syntactic dimensions of word representations generated by neural language models, specifically focusing on how they encode Loughran-McDonald (LM) sentiment polarities. We evaluate these representations using various metrics, including cosine similarity, linear classifiers, and non-linear neural networks. Our findings indicate that while current word representations capture certain aspects of LM polarities, they fail to fully comprehend the underlying semantics and syntax of these polarity tags.

This paper introduces SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM adaptations of a previously developed broadband waveform designed for simultaneous data and power transmission. These new formats retain the key advantages of the original system—specifically its robustness against variations in the power-line impedance and its ability to function without prior knowledge of the receiver's characteristics—while offering the performance benefits inherent to multiple antennas and orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing.

This study introduces a novel numerical framework utilizing combined level-set and embedded boundary methods to solve interface tracking problems involving solidification and melting. The approach employs an embedded boundary technique to define the solid-liquid interface, while the level-set function serves to determine the associated boundary conditions. This integration allows for the accurate computation of temperature and heat flux across the interface, even when the interface normal is not aligned with the computational grid. The methodology is validated through two benchmark cases: a single sphere melting in an infinite domain and a sphere melting within a finite domain.

This paper addresses the challenge of generating a set of training examples for a specific multiplayer game, enabling a designated player to learn a strategy that constitutes a rationalizable equilibrium within that game. We introduce a novel algorithm designed to construct such training datasets, which are subsequently used to train the designated player via reinforcement learning. Our approach guarantees that the resulting player adheres to a strategy satisfying the requirements of a rationalizable equilibrium. We validate our method through experiments on a three-player competitive environment, demonstrating that the trained player achieves a rationalizable equilibrium and outperforms baseline approaches.

This study examines epidemic dynamics on networks where individuals can implement protective rewiring to alter their connections. We introduce a mathematical framework that integrates both epidemic transmission and the strategic rewiring of the network, analyzing it through the lens of an evolutionary game to determine the system's steady states. Our research reveals that the interplay between transmission and rewiring mechanisms can generate complex, non-monotonic dynamics. Specifically, increasing the cost of rewiring may unexpectedly elevate the epidemic's final size. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the model supports a "tipping point" phenomenon: a slight increase in rewiring efficacy can trigger a sudden, drastic reduction in the epidemic's final size.

This paper introduces a novel, unified theory framework designed to guide the modification of parton distribution functions (PDFs). This approach integrates the established principles of PDF fitting with the rigorous requirements of Bayesian model selection, specifically utilizing the Deviance Information Criterion (DIC) to evaluate the impact of new data and theoretical inputs. The framework is applied to assess recent datasets, including LHC measurements of top quark pair production and LHCb results on forward $Z$ boson production, alongside older global fits. The analysis reveals that while the new data significantly enhances the precision of PDF parameters, it does not necessarily improve the overall quality of the fit. Furthermore, the study highlights that the inclusion of LHCb findings is highly sensitive to the choice of prior distributions, a crucial insight for future PDF fitting initiatives.

This study introduces Variance Decrease based Experience Replay (VDER), a novel algorithm designed to enhance the sample efficiency of off-policy reinforcement learning. VDER functions by selecting replay samples based on the variance of their importance sampling ratios, specifically prioritizing those exhibiting high variance. This strategy aims to mitigate the variance inherent in off-policy updates while simultaneously ensuring that the replay buffer remains representative of the current distribution. Empirical evaluations across various environments demonstrate that VDER outperforms existing methods in both sample efficiency and final performance.

This paper introduces MultiTalk, a novel branching dialogue framework designed to handle diverse conversational flows. Unlike traditional methods that rely on rigid, linear interactions, MultiTalk enables users to navigate multiple conversation paths simultaneously, allowing the system to branch out based on user input. This architecture supports varied dialogue trajectories, ensuring the system can adapt to different topics and user needs. By facilitating these branching structures, MultiTalk creates a more dynamic and flexible conversation experience, moving beyond the limitations of fixed linear sequences.

We introduce a new class of modified gravity theories known as conformal linking models, which are defined by a scalar field and a vector field where the latter mediates interactions between the former and the metric. We derive the complete set of field equations for these models and demonstrate that they can be solved numerically using a standard N-body simulation framework. To validate this approach, we conduct simulations of a specific model previously studied by Li, Li, and Dodelson (2012), which features a negative coupling between the scalar field and matter. Our results confirm that this model successfully reproduces the observed cosmic acceleration and the growth of cosmic structure. Furthermore, we establish that the numerical method is applicable to any conformal linking model, enabling researchers to rapidly assess the viability of various modified gravity scenarios through N-body simulations.

We examine the coupling of Gaussian free fields (GFIs) with multiple Schramm-Loewner evolutions (SLEs) driven by random log-gases. By leveraging the probabilistic structure of these log-gases, we establish the existence of a specific class of multiple SLEs characterized by interaction parameters $\chi$ and $\xi$. These processes are defined as the solutions to stochastic differential equations (SDEs) where the driving forces are explicitly determined by the interaction parameters. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the joint distribution of the trajectories generated by these processes can be expressed as a Schur polynomial.

WorkingWiki is an open-source, free wiki system built as a MediaWiki extension, specifically designed to function as a shared workspace for research teams. It offers a suite of features that streamline collaborative efforts, including integrated task lists, a calendar system, and a dedicated area for project-specific news. Additionally, WorkingWiki introduces a novel "research object" concept, which serves as a standardized container for organizing and managing research-related artifacts. This platform aims to enhance efficiency by centralizing tools and documentation essential for collective inquiry.

This study employs a linearized framework to simulate the reaction of a turbulent jet fire to acoustic excitation, utilizing an active flame method. This approach integrates a linearized RANS-based jet model with a linearized G-equation to represent the flame front. The jet model incorporates a linearized Reynolds stress term to account for turbulent mixing effects on the mean flow, while the flame front is treated as a discontinuity in the mean flow properties. The research focuses on a vertical jet fire interacting with a horizontal acoustic duct, with the flame positioned at the jet exit. The simulation results are benchmarked against experimental data from the CEA, demonstrating excellent agreement in predicting the mean flow, turbulent mixing, and the response to acoustic excitation.

We examine the impact of interactions between neutrinos and ultralight dark matter (DM) on neutrinoless double-beta ($0\nu\beta\beta$) decay and astrophysical processes. We demonstrate that such encounters can significantly alter the $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay rate, potentially shifting the predicted half-life by several orders of magnitude. Furthermore, we explore how these interactions influence supernova dynamics and the emission of neutrinos from the early universe, concluding with an assessment of the observational constraints on these effects.

This paper examines the nonlocal gravitational theory introduced by the authors in 2019, which relies on a constitutive relation linking the affine connection to the energy-momentum tensor. We demonstrate that this connection is not merely auxiliary but constitutes a fundamental field within the theory's geometric framework. By deriving the theory's action and field equations, we establish a direct parallel with the standard Einstein-Cartan formalism, identifying the new constitutive connection as a specific type of spin connection. Furthermore, we prove that this nonlocal gravity model is mathematically equivalent to an Einstein-Cartan theory featuring a nonlocal spin-torsion coupling. Finally, we explore the implications of this framework for the description of black holes.

This study investigates the integration of functional genomic data with genome-wide association study (GWAS) results for eight human traits. We introduce a novel statistical framework designed to assess the impact of functional annotations on GWAS findings. This framework employs a hierarchical Bayesian approach to evaluate the probability that a specific genomic region contains a trait-influencing variant, utilizing both GWAS summary statistics and functional annotations. We demonstrate the method's efficacy through simulations and an analysis of 18 traits, including height, body mass index, and schizophrenia. Furthermore, we present a user-friendly R package named fGWAS to facilitate the application of this methodology.

The production of small, high-energy systems at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) can be achieved through proton-antiproton collisions, proton-nucleus interactions, or proton-proton collisions at low multiplicity. This review examines the experimental capabilities and theoretical frameworks relevant to these systems, with a specific focus on the ALICE experiment.

We examine the repetition intervals of transient events in Galactic Centre X-ray binaries, specifically analyzing the 1.4-year interval of the well-known source GRS 1738+24. We argue that this interval is not a coincidence but a manifestation of a broader phenomenon affecting the entire Galactic Centre population of dormant X-ray binaries. We propose that these systems are synchronized by a 1.4-year cycle, which represents the maximum duration these sources can remain undetected. This synchronization hypothesis aligns with the observed clustering of transient outbursts in the last decade and offers a coherent explanation for the lack of such events in the Milky Way's disk.

Momentum transfer to a molecule's vibrational modes can significantly influence the electronic and spin characteristics of a molecule. This study introduces a theoretical framework for analyzing electron-vibrational and spin-vibrational interactions mediated by momentum transfer. We derive analytical expressions for momentum-dependent electron-vibrational coupling constants and demonstrate that this effect can substantially alter electron-vibrational interactions. Furthermore, we show that momentum transfer induces novel spin-vibrational coupling mechanisms, which are distinct from traditional electron-vibrational interactions. These findings offer new insights into the impact of molecular vibrations on electronic and spin properties and may inform the design of advanced molecular devices.

This study introduces a novel Natural Language Inference (NLI) task designed to assess semantic diversity in textual discourse. We posit that an NLI model should classify a pair of texts as "entailment" only when the second text conveys information that is both inferable from and distinct from what is already present in the first. To train our model, we constructed a dataset of 100,000 pairs of news article introductions and their corresponding lead sentences, manually annotated with entailment labels. Furthermore, we developed a new dataset comprising 10,000 pairs of distinct, high-quality sentences drawn from news articles to serve as positive examples of variety. These were contrasted with 10,000 pairs of unlabelled texts, from which we selected the top 50,000 based on model confidence to form a negative training set. We present the resulting 100,000-sample dataset, named DISCOTEXT, and evaluate the model's performance on various benchmarks, including the aforementioned variety corpus, the XSum dataset, and the original SNLI dataset.

We have conducted numerical simulations to investigate the structural evolution of rotating substellar objects, ranging from massive brown dwarfs to massive planets, as they approach the mass-shedding limit. These objects are modeled using a realistic equation of state that accounts for partial ionization and molecular hydrogen formation, alongside a radiative transfer scheme based on the diffusion approximation. Our results indicate that the maximum rotation period decreases significantly as total mass increases; for instance, a $0.01\,M_{\odot}$ object can reach the mass-shedding limit at approximately $1.5$ times the breakup rate, whereas a $1\,M_{\mathrm{Jup}}$ object is limited to roughly $0.8$ times this rate.
