It details the diverse array of mental health disorders prevalent in prisons, including substance abuse, depression, anxiety, and personality disorders, while also addressing the necessity of such care. The paper outlines mandatory therapy protocols across various jurisdictions, exploring the arguments both supporting and opposing compulsory treatment. Furthermore, it investigates the efficacy of these programs, the challenges associated with their implementation, and the role of voluntary participation. The research highlights the critical importance of addressing mental well-being within the penal system, emphasizing that compulsory therapy serves as a vital component of rehabilitation and reintegration efforts. Ultimately, the work underscores the necessity for continued investigation into these initiatives to enhance their effectiveness and assist incarcerated populations in achieving successful societal re-entry.

This study introduces a novel regularization method designed to enhance the segmentation of medical images, utilizing a framework built upon the "Awkward" library. This approach employs consistency regularization, which enforces uniformity across multiple data augmentations of the same image. To achieve this, the method utilizes a lightweight, parameter-free convolutional neural network (CNN) to generate initial segmentations, which then guide the primary segmentation model. We evaluated our approach on two distinct medical image datasets: the ACDC cardiac dataset and the Pancreas dataset. The results indicate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art semi-supervised techniques, achieving superior performance even when trained with only 10 annotated images. Furthermore, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the model's behavior regarding data augmentation strategies and the primary CNN architecture.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as a powerful tool for analyzing complex systems, offering a distinct advantage over traditional methods by requiring no prior knowledge of the underlying system's dynamics. This study introduces a novel GNN architecture designed to model Hamiltonian systems, which are defined by their reversible and deterministic evolution. The proposed framework successfully reconstructs the system's phase space trajectories directly from time series data of position and momentum, even when the initial conditions are unknown. Furthermore, the method estimates the Kolmogorov-Sinai (KS) entropy—a metric for chaos—by leveraging the reconstructed phase space without needing to know the specific equations of motion. The approach is validated through simulations of various systems, including the Hénon-Heiles model, the kicked rotor, and the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam chain. Finally, the paper presents a new, intuitive visualization technique for KS entropy that relies on the learned graph structure.

This study introduces a generalized maximum likelihood (GML) approach for estimating the average value of a population when data comes from a mixture of different sampling methods. This GML framework extends the standard maximum likelihood (ML) method, which is typically used when all data originates from a single sampling technique. The paper details how to construct the associated likelihood function and outlines the specific conditions required for the resulting GML estimators to be consistent and asymptotically normal. Finally, the authors apply this methodology to a real-world scenario involving the estimation of the average credit card balance across various demographic groups, utilizing data drawn from multiple distinct sampling strategies.

Knowledge Tracing (KT) is a student modeling technique that estimates a learner's proficiency by analyzing their historical interactions with educational materials. Deep learning-based KT methods have gained popularity due to their superior performance compared to traditional approaches; however, the rapid emergence of numerous new models has made it difficult to evaluate them effectively. This proliferation has led to inconsistent benchmarking practices, where different studies utilize varying datasets, training protocols, and evaluation metrics, thereby hindering fair model comparison. To resolve these issues, we introduce pyKT, a unified Python framework designed to standardize the evaluation of deep learning-based KT systems. pyKT offers a modular architecture that streamlines the development of new models and ensures reproducible experiments. We demonstrate its utility by implementing and assessing ten state-of-the-art KT models across three distinct datasets. Furthermore, we address common pitfalls in KT evaluation, such as data leakage and improper train-test splitting, and provide practical guidance for robust benchmarking. pyKT is released as open-source software under the MIT license at https://github.com/pyKT/pyKT.

This paper demonstrates that the range of the elliptic operator $P$ on a manifold $M$ is constrained by the cohomology groups of $M$. Specifically, if $P$ is a second-order differential operator with constant coefficients acting on $n$-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, and its symbol $\sigma(P)$ is non-degenerate on the cotangent bundle $T^*\mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{0\}$, then $P$ admits a right inverse on $\mathbb{R}^n$ that maps $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ to itself for all $1 < p < \infty$. Furthermore, when $M$ is a manifold of dimension $n$ and $P$ is a second-order operator with constant coefficients on $M$ such that its symbol $\sigma(P)$ remains non-degenerate on $T^*M \setminus \{0\}$, the range of $P$ on $C^\infty(M)$ is characterized by specific cohomology groups of $M$.

This paper introduces the EVC (Evidence Verification Code) format, a new standard designed to encapsulate proof objects generated by SMT solvers. The primary objective of EVC is to facilitate the exchange of proof data among diverse verification tools, thereby streamlining the process of validating proofs across various environments. To achieve this, EVC functions as a binary format that supports extensibility, allowing for the inclusion of custom proof rules and tactics. The development of EVC was driven by the need to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of proof validation within the context of the CVC3 proof checker.

This study examines the Federated Gradient Descent (FGD) algorithm, which trains deep neural networks across distributed clients using synchronous data-parallelism. We demonstrate that, under specific conditions, FGD functions as an unconstrained gradient descent method with a modified step size, even when it lacks the typical assumption of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data. This finding allows us to apply existing convergence guarantees for unconstrained gradient descent to analyze FGD. Furthermore, we introduce a buffered variant of FGD that incorporates a gradient accumulator, proving it to be an unconstrained gradient descent algorithm with averaged steps. These theoretical contributions yield new convergence bounds for both standard and buffered FGD, which are empirically validated against state-of-the-art results.

This study introduces and evaluates Rough2Detail, a novel framework designed to enhance cross- and interdomain automatic speech recognition (ASR) performance. The approach functions in two stages: initially, it synthesizes detailed, high-quality transcripts from coarse, noisy translations of multilingual, expert-curated parallel corpora; subsequently, these enriched datasets are employed to train robust cross- and interdomain ASR models. Experiments conducted across multiple languages and domains demonstrate that Rough2Detail significantly boosts ASR accuracy when addressing challenging cross- and interdomain tasks.

This study introduces a novel approach to enhance marine robot navigation by addressing the challenge of temporal variation in Gaussian process (GP) reward functions. While GPs are widely adopted for reinforcement learning (RL) due to their ability to model uncertainty, they often struggle with the high sample counts required for RL, leading to suboptimal policies. Furthermore, the performance of these policies frequently degrades when environmental conditions shift over time. To tackle these issues, we propose a method that injects temporal variation into the GP reward function, thereby improving RL performance under changing environments. Our approach models the time-dependent reward function as a sparse GP with temporal variation, allowing the robot to learn an effective policy using fewer samples while maintaining robustness against environmental shifts. We validate our method through simulations of a marine robot navigating a dynamic underwater setting, demonstrating its efficacy in learning optimal policies despite temporal variations in the reward landscape.

This study examines the static, spherically symmetric configurations of two-fluid celestial bodies under the assumption of hydrostatic equilibrium for each component. We derive the governing field equations and present a novel, unified formulation for the system's solutions. This approach allows for the construction of various non-uniform solutions by integrating a single master function, which is defined by an arbitrary source term. We specifically investigate a case where this source term is linear, yielding a closed-form solution featuring a power-law density profile for one fluid and a corresponding power-law behavior for the other. We also analyze the physical characteristics of this specific solution and compare it against a model of two uniform fluids. Finally, we perform a comparative study of our non-uniform model with an existing model of a non-uniform dark matter core surrounded by uniform dark and baryonic matter.

Automatic Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) is a text processing task that rectifies grammatical mistakes in written English. While current state-of-the-art models have significantly advanced, they still require extensive training data to achieve high performance. This study introduces a few-shot domain transfer learning method designed to boost the effectiveness of GEC models when applied to new, unseen domains. We employ a meta-learning framework to train a generic GEC model capable of rapidly adapting to specific target domains using only a few annotated examples. Our approach involves training on multiple source domains to create a generalizable base model, which is subsequently fine-tuned with minimal data from a new target domain. We evaluated our method on four distinct domains, including two previously unexplored ones, and compared the results against several strong baselines. The experiments demonstrate that our proposed technique outperforms existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving very limited target domain data.

This paper investigates the allocation of indivisible resources among strategic agents who possess distinct valuations, aiming to analyze the relationship between Nash equilibria and equity. We demonstrate that in a broad class of valuation functions, Nash equilibria are inherently inequitable, as the disparity between the most and least advantaged agents grows without bound as the number of agents increases. Furthermore, we examine the trade-off between equity and social welfare within this framework.

This study presents new H$\alpha$ and CO(1-0) observations of the star-forming galaxy UGC 8839, which exhibits a prominent, luminous, and spatially extended disk of star formation located well beyond its visible stellar disk. We utilized these datasets to construct a rotation curve, revealing that the system remains dynamically supported by gas out to approximately 10 effective radii ($R_e$). Furthermore, we derived a new mass model incorporating a dark matter halo, a stellar component, and a bulge, which indicates that the extended star-forming disk resides in a region dominated by dark matter. Despite this, the circular velocity within the extended disk is exceptionally high, reaching roughly 250 km s$^{-1}$ at 10 $R_e$. This velocity is comparable to the escape velocity, suggesting the disk is ultra-stable and likely gravitationally bound. Additionally, the high rotation speeds imply that the gas in this extended disk possesses very low specific angular momentum relative to its mass. Finally, we compared these findings with other galaxies hosting extended disks, concluding that the extended disk of UGC 8839 is likely a transient structure resulting from a recent accretion event.

This study examines the pion's two-current correlation function within lattice QCD using $N_f=2+1$ Wilson fermions at physical quark masses. By analyzing the spatial and temporal dependencies of this function, we extract the pion's charge and axial radii. Our findings indicate that the charge radius squared, $\langle r^2\rangle_a$, is approximately 0.25 fm$^2$ larger than the charge radius squared, $\langle r^2\rangle_c$, which aligns with previous results. Furthermore, we observe a distinct difference between these radii in the isospin-symmetric limit, a feature absent in earlier investigations.

T Tauri stars are known for exhibiting irregular accretion fluctuations, yet the extreme nature of these events remains difficult to characterize. This study analyzes a 10-year optical dataset of XX Cha, a T Tauri star previously identified as having the lowest accretion rate among those with observed outburges. The data reveals that XX Cha experienced a significant accretion outburst approximately 1.5 years after the last event recorded in earlier research. Furthermore, the analysis indicates that the star's accretion rate fluctuates on timescales ranging from days to years, with the most recent outburst reaching a magnitude roughly 1 dex higher than the peak seen previously. These findings demonstrate that even stars with low accretion rates can undergo extreme accretion events, suggesting that current estimates of the maximum accretion rate variability may be underrepresented.

Offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has recently gained traction, offering a pathway to scale up multi-agent systems by learning from historical data. However, existing methods face significant hurdles: they often require unrealistic assumptions about data generation, struggle with sparse positive outcomes, and lack the ability to generalize across different environments. To address these issues, we introduce Off-Policy Multi-Agent Trajectory Learning (OMTL), a novel off-policy framework designed to learn from sparse positive trajectories. Unlike prior approaches, OMTL requires no assumptions regarding the data generator and functions effectively even when only a single positive trajectory is available. Furthermore, OMTL demonstrates the ability to generalize to unseen states. Our theoretical analysis provides bounds for both value and policy generalization, while extensive experiments confirm that OMTL outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in sparse positive trajectory learning and generalization tasks.

This study introduces a novel 2D/3D image registration method designed to align 2D megavoltage (MV) images with 3D computed tomography (CT) scans, aiming to enhance the accuracy of radiotherapy treatment planning. The proposed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture learns a non-linear mapping between 2D MV images and 3D volumes, generating a synthetic 3D dataset that serves as a prior for guiding the alignment of actual MV images. To achieve this, the network employs a 3D convolutional layer to extract features from the 2D MV input, followed by a 3D convolutional layer that integrates these features with those derived from the original CT scan. The generated synthetic 3D data is then utilized to initialize the optimization process for actual MV-to-CT registration. Experiments conducted on a dataset of 100 patients demonstrate that this CNN-based approach significantly outperforms standard optimization techniques, achieving a reduction in mean squared displacement (MSD) by 30% to 50% compared to conventional methods.

We introduce a new class of entangled states defined by the single-particle formalism, which are characterized by the fact that no individual particle can be described by a single-particle state vector. We demonstrate that these states produce genuine nonlocal effects, specifically manifesting as the Bohmian guidance law for both particles within an EPR setup. This finding suggests that single-particle entanglement serves as a distinct and potent resource for generating nonlocality.

The rapid advancement of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) has enabled the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) to facilitate extensive data sharing among connected vehicles, thereby enhancing overall traffic efficiency. However, the massive scale of data generated by IoV applications presents significant challenges regarding storage, security, and privacy. To address these issues, this paper introduces a Blockchain-enabled Federated Education framework for IoV. This proposed framework integrates Federated Learning (FL) and Blockchain technologies to ensure secure data sharing, robust privacy protection, and efficient model training. The study provides a comprehensive analysis of Blockchain-assisted FL within IoV environments, categorizing existing research into three primary groups: Blockchain-aided FL for secure data sharing, privacy preservation, and federated model training. Finally, the paper outlines the proposed framework's design and identifies key open challenges for future investigation.

V392 Persei, a well-documented dwarf nova that experienced a nova eruption in 1999, was recently identified as a nova outburst via gamma-ray emissions. This event marks the first instance of a nova eruption from a known cataclysmic variable star with a low mass accretion rate to be detected in gamma rays. The outburst was characterized using data from the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, Swift satellite, and ground-based observatories. Spectral analysis of the gamma-ray emissions indicates that the radiation originates from a non-thermal population of electrons within a shock structure located in the accretion disk wind. Furthermore, the observed gamma-ray luminosity, when compared to the bolometric luminosity, suggests that the shock in this event is significantly more powerful than those seen in other novae outbursts.

This paper introduces a novel feedback encoding scheme designed to enhance the performance of multi-antenna systems by encoding feedback information within a Golay-Complementary Code (GCC) framework. The proposed method leverages Golay-Complementary Codes (GCCs) to facilitate the construction of a codebook, which is subsequently employed for feedback encoding. The feedback process involves transmitting the indices of Golay pairs selected from the codebook to the base station. Upon receiving these indices, the base station reconstructs the original feedback matrix by combining the corresponding Golay pairs. The paper details the derivation of this Golay-based codebook and analyzes its efficacy through simulations, demonstrating that the proposed scheme achieves performance comparable to existing codebook feedback methods while offering the distinct advantage of reduced feedback overhead.

We investigate the dynamics of a charged particle moving in a three-dimensional cubic lattice under a uniform magnetic field and stochastic forces, focusing on the diffusion characteristics across the entire Hofstadter spectrum. Our analysis reveals that, contrary to expectations, diffusion remains anomalous across most of the spectrum, with surface flows identified as the primary cause. These robust flows persist even when the particle experiences significant stochasticity, a feature that distinguishes them from previously documented phenomena. We further demonstrate that these surface flows are topologically protected, a property directly linked to the Chern numbers associated with the Hofstadter bands.

This work establishes a constraint on the rate of Bondi mass loss within a specific class of asymptotically flat spacetimes. By analyzing the Bondi-Sachs metric under the conditions of vacuum Einstein equations, asymptotic flatness, and spherical symmetry, we derive a differential inequality governing the Bondi mass function $m(u,r)$, where $u$ denotes the retarded time and $r$ represents the radial coordinate. Integrating this inequality yields an upper bound on the rate of Bondi mass loss, expressed as $\left|\frac{dm}{du}\right| \leqslant \frac{C}{r^2}$, with $C$ being a positive constant. This finding indicates that the reduction of Bondi mass cannot occur arbitrarily rapidly. Furthermore, we examine the scenario where this rate reaches its maximum limit, demonstrating that the system approaches a linearized Schwarzschild spacetime characterized by a time-dependent mass function.

We examine the formation of massive binaries within nuclear star clusters (NSCs) and globular clusters (GCs), focusing on their role in generating gravitational waves (GWs) from the remnants of the initial stellar population. Our analysis indicates that in both GCs and NSCs, the formation of massive binaries is significantly hindered by dynamical interactions, which disrupt hardening processes and prevent the creation of compact object binaries capable of merging. Consequently, GW emission from these systems is negligible in GCs. However, in NSCs, this emission may be substantial, contingent upon the specific binary formation mechanism operating in these environments.

This study introduces a novel multi-carrier wireless system designed for secure communication, utilizing an architecture where an auxiliary relay station assists in data transmission. The setup involves a source node transmitting confidential information to a destination via $K$ orthogonal subcarriers, supported by the relay. To ensure security, the source allocates transmit power adaptively across these carriers based on the instantaneous channel conditions of both the source-destination and source-relay links. The source-destination channels experience independent Rayleigh fading, while the source-relay channels are modeled as deterministic. The objective is to maximize the system's secrecy throughput, defined as the total achievable data rate on secure carriers, subject to constraints on average transmit power and a minimum required rate for each subcarrier. The resulting non-convex optimization problem is addressed by deriving its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions and formulating an efficient iterative algorithm to identify the optimal power allocation strategy. Numerical simulations validate the proposed approach, demonstrating that the system achieves the targeted performance metrics.

Text games serve as an engaging and accessible medium for developing artificial general intelligence, yet their widespread adoption is hindered by the high computational costs associated with game simulation. To address this bottleneck, we introduce TextWorldExpress, a high-performance C++ engine designed to render these games at extreme speeds. By leveraging advanced techniques such as memory-mapped file I/O, optimized rendering, and multithreading, TextWorldExpress achieves a simulation rate exceeding one million game moves per second. This performance represents a 100-fold increase compared to standard Python implementations. Consequently, this system enables the execution of Monte Carlo Tree Search algorithms on the full, unmodified TextWorld environment, facilitating the training of agents that surpass human-level performance.

This study introduces a hardware and algorithm co-development framework designed to deploy energy-efficient Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for video-based object recognition. The proposed architecture leverages Hierarchical Tucker Tensor Decomposition (HTTD) to execute matrix multiplications, thereby reducing memory bandwidth usage and computational load. Furthermore, the design incorporates a novel, high-bandwidth memory subsystem optimized for the specific data access patterns generated by HTTD operations. Experimental results demonstrate that this architecture achieves a 100-fold reduction in energy consumption compared to conventional implementations.

We examine the feeble gravity conjecture within the framework of the convexity of charged states in conformal field theories (CFTs). We establish that this conjecture holds for a broad class of free theories, including those with $U(1)$ symmetry, and we propose a generalization of the $c$-theorem that supports the conjecture in two dimensions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the conjecture is violated in certain non-supersymmetric $\mathbb{C}P^{N}$ models, as well as in specific $O(N)$ models at large $N$ and small charges. Finally, we explore the relationship between this conjecture and the W-gap conjecture.

This study introduces a novel framework for procuring auxiliary services within electricity markets, designed to address the growing demand for such services in policy-making. The model explicitly incorporates the engagement levels of both market participants and regulators, allowing for the assessment of how these factors influence service procurement outcomes. By analyzing the resulting market equilibrium, the research offers strategic guidance for participants and actionable recommendations for regulators. Furthermore, the paper explores the impact of varying degrees of market engagement on the procurement process. The findings indicate that heightened engagement from either market players or regulators can significantly alter the market equilibrium, thereby reshaping the procurement of auxiliary services.

This paper investigates the primality of $f(g(n)) + 1$, where $f$ and $g$ are polynomials with integer coefficients. We establish that $f(g(n)) + 1$ is prime for infinitely many values of $n$ under specific conditions on $f$ and $g$. Conversely, we demonstrate that if $f$ and $g$ satisfy certain other conditions, $f(g(n)) + 1$ can be prime only finitely often.

Saturn's northern polar region has been the site of a massive atmospheric vortex for over a decade, yet it has only recently developed into a hurricane-like storm comparable to Jupiter's Great Red Spot. This paper presents new observations from the Keck II telescope, utilizing the NIRC2 instrument and advanced adaptive optics, which reveal a hexagonal cloud pattern forming around Saturn's north pole at approximately 66.5 degrees latitude. This feature emerged during the early stages of the polar vortex's development, roughly one year prior to the solstice, and persisted for at least another year. The study details the discovery, analyzes the feature's characteristics, and discusses its potential significance regarding the formation of Saturn's polar vortex.

This study examines the initial value problem for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation in exterior domains, featuring a convex obstacle and focusing on the $L^2$-critical case where the nonlinearity exponent is $p=3$. We establish that for initial data with sufficiently large amplitude, the solution blows up in finite time within the energy space. This result is derived by applying a novel, robust blow-up criterion applicable to both defocusing and focusing variants of the equation.

This paper examines the concept of local-uniform semi-parametric abbreviations, which are defined as collections of positive-characteristic polynomials that define varieties over $\mathbb{Q}$-algebras. We establish that if a variety is semi-parametrically locally uniformly abbreviated, it is also semi-parametrically finitely generated. Conversely, we demonstrate that not every variety which is semi-parametrically finitely generated can be semi-parametrically locally uniformly abbreviated.

This paper examines the relationship between two distinct methods for extending measures from locally compact groups to their abelianization. We establish that these extensions are equivalent provided the original measure adheres to specific conditions regarding its behavior on orbits. Furthermore, we introduce a generalized class of orbits and demonstrate that any measure satisfying these new constraints ensures the two extension methods remain consistent.

Nuclear phase recovery spectroscopy (NPRS) is a novel technique that leverages x-ray absorption spectroscopy to precisely measure the energy levels of nuclear excited states. This method achieves exceptional resolution by combining the natural narrowness of nuclear transitions with the high energy selectivity of x-ray Raman scattering. Currently, the primary constraint on NPRS performance is the relatively low scattering cross-section of x-ray Raman processes. This limitation can be significantly alleviated by employing x-ray Raman scattering at the K-edge of the target element, where the cross-section is enhanced by a factor of approximately 100 due to resonant scattering. In this study, we introduce a new variant of NPRS based on resonant x-ray Raman scattering. We detail the fundamental principles of this approach and present initial experimental results obtained using the 23Na isotope. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of the method and suggest that future experiments could achieve a resolution surpassing 100 eV.

This study introduces a novel finite element framework designed to model single-phase fluid flow within fractured porous media, utilizing the Discrete Fracture Model (DFM). The proposed method integrates a standard finite element approach for the continuous porous domain with a hybrid finite element scheme for the fracture network. This integration allows the method to accurately represent the complex coupling conditions at the interfaces between the matrix and the fractures. The resulting system of algebraic equations is solved using an iterative algorithm. Numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the method's efficacy, specifically highlighting its ability to handle the numerical challenges associated with the high contrast in permeability between the matrix and the fractures.

Bayes factors serve as a robust tool for statistical inference, offering a clear method to evaluate the evidence supporting or against the null hypothesis. However, their widespread application is often hindered by the substantial computational resources required to conduct the extensive simulations necessary for estimating the marginal likelihood. This paper introduces a suite of workflows designed to maximize the utility of Bayes factors by integrating them with advanced computational techniques, including parallel processing, high-performance computing, and cloud computing. The authors provide practical guidance on implementing these strategies and illustrate their effectiveness through a case study involving a two-sample t-test.

Discourse markers, such as *well*, *you know*, and *actually*, are frequently employed to regulate the flow of conversation and are often associated with non-native English proficiency. While existing research has primarily concentrated on the linguistic features surrounding these markers, this study introduces a novel approach by analyzing the semantic roles they play within discourse. To achieve this, we developed DiscSense, a system that automatically categorizes discourse markers into six distinct semantic classes: *additive, adversative, causal, temporal, emphatic,* and *phatic*. We evaluated DiscSense using a manually annotated dataset of 1,000 instances drawn from the news domain of the New York Times, achieving an F1 score of 81.3%. Furthermore, we conducted a case study on a corpus of 100,000 words from the New York Times to examine how these markers function semantically in news reporting. Our analysis indicates that these indicators are utilized to structure information, facilitate transitions between topics, and highlight key points.

We introduce a novel methodology to investigate the worldwide geometry of optimization landscapes for nonconvex matrix problems, utilizing Riemannian manifold concepts. This approach allows us to analyze the problem from a Riemannian perspective, which is essential for handling the nonconvex nature of these tasks. By integrating these manifold-based techniques, we gain deeper insights into the global structure of the optimization problem. Our study focuses on the nonconvex geometry of the problem, which is analyzed through the lens of Riemannian manifolds. This specific viewpoint is chosen because it provides the necessary tools to effectively address the inherent complexities and challenges associated with nonconvex matrix problems. Ultimately, this Riemannian framework offers a rigorous way to explore the global geometry of the problem, revealing key features that might be obscured by traditional Euclidean analysis.

In 2021, Foucaud, Havet, and Thomasson introduced the concept of total edge colorings with robustness, demonstrating that for any integer $k \geq 2$ and any cubic bipartite graph $G$, there exists a $(k+1)$-edge coloring such that no monochromatic cycle of length at most $2k$ can be formed by swapping two edges of identical color. This paper investigates cubic bipartite graphs $G$ where a $(k+1)$-edge coloring exists, ensuring that no monochromatic cycle of length at most $2k$ arises from any single edge color swap. We establish that for every $k \geq 2$, there is a cubic bipartite graph $G$ for which the maximum number of forbidden cycle lengths, denoted as $s(G)$, satisfies $s(G) \leq 2k$. Furthermore, we prove that for any cubic graph $G$ with a perfect matching, $s(G) \leq 2k$.

This study introduces a coevolutionary genetic algorithm designed to determine Nash Equilibrium (NE) in a symmetric Cournot oligopoly featuring a linear demand curve and constant marginal costs. In this framework, each agent in the population represents a single firm and possesses a genetic makeup that dictates its production strategy. Agents interact within a well-mixed population, and their fitness is evaluated based on individual profits. Firms with higher fitness are selected for reproduction, generating offspring that inherit traits from parents while undergoing mutations. The proposed algorithm operates in discrete time steps, where the population size doubles at each iteration; consequently, the total population expands exponentially over time. The research analyzes the asymptotic behavior of this system as the population approaches infinity, demonstrating that the algorithm converges to a unique NE. Furthermore, the study provides a rigorous mathematical proof of the algorithm's convergence and validates its performance through numerical simulations.

This paper investigates the shared and distinctive attributes of edge ideals associated with weighted directed graphs. Specifically, we identify conditions under which these ideals exhibit both common and unique Betti table structures.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have become the standard for computer vision tasks, yet their susceptibility to adversarial attacks remains a significant concern. While existing research has explored various defenses, this paper introduces a novel approach to mitigate such threats by detecting hardware malfunctions. We propose a method that identifies these failures through the observation of activation ranges within neural network layers. Our strategy involves training a separate, lightweight "range network" to predict the expected activation range for any given input image. During inference, the system compares these predictions against actual activations; significant deviations trigger an alert indicating a potential hardware fault. We evaluated our approach on ImageNet using ResNet-50 and VGG-16 architectures. Results demonstrate that our method effectively detects both white-box and black-box adversarial attacks, as well as hardware-induced noise, with minimal computational overhead. Furthermore, we conducted extensive experiments on real-world hardware to validate the technique's practicality.

This work presents a one-parameter family of Jordanian twists, which, when applied to the enveloping enveloping of the Heisenberg algebra, yields the Drinfeld twist associated with the enveloping enveloping of the affine $\mathfrak{u}(1)$-current algebra. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this parameterized collection encompasses the specific case previously identified by Reshetikhin, Takhtajan, and Faddeev.

This study introduces a novel multi-lingual shared semantic framework designed to facilitate cross-lingual natural language processing. The proposed method constructs a unified semantic space for diverse languages by projecting word embeddings from each language into a common space, ensuring that words with similar meanings across languages are positioned adjacently. To achieve this, the approach optimizes a cluster-consistent objective function, which aligns the internal cluster structures of word clusters within the shared space with those in the original embedding spaces. We evaluated the framework's efficacy on both supervised and unsupervised cross-lingual text classification tasks, demonstrating significant performance improvements compared to existing methods.

This study presents new measurements of pion, kaon, (anti-)proton, and $\phi$ meson production in Xe-Xe collisions at the CERN Large Hadron Collider, conducted at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.44$ TeV. Data were collected using the ALICE detector, encompassing a wide range of multiplicity classes. The results provide essential input for interpreting recent findings on the elliptic flow of identified particles, which were recently reported in the same system. Furthermore, these data enable the reconstruction of the particle-to-particle correlation across various centrality levels, thereby facilitating the extraction of the initial spatial anisotropy in the transverse plane. This analysis allows for a direct comparison with results obtained from Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV. Additionally, the study examines the dependence of particle yields on transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) and compares them against theoretical predictions derived from the AMPT and EPOS models.

In the aftermath of the 2019 Chilean protests, which were triggered by a subway fare increase but quickly escalated into widespread civil unrest, this study introduces a novel epidemiological non-global model designed to simulate the dynamics of such disturbances. The framework incorporates a heterogeneous population divided into distinct compartments representing various social roles, alongside a specific compartment for individuals who have left the country. By integrating a migration term into the system, the authors derive the basic reproduction number ($R_0$) and establish conditions for the existence of both disease-free and endemic equilibria. Furthermore, the research investigates the local and global stability of these equilibria. The findings indicate that the disease-free equilibrium remains locally stable when $R_0$ is less than one, whereas the system exhibits the emergence of an endemic state when $R_0$ exceeds this threshold. Finally, the paper presents numerical simulations that validate the theoretical results and illustrate the model's behavior.

This paper introduces EMA-VIO, a novel visual-inertial navigation framework designed to overcome the limitations of conventional methods, which often suffer from accumulated drift and susceptibility to environmental noise. To address these challenges, EMA-VIO employs an Externally Memory Attention (EMA) mechanism that dynamically integrates historical trajectory data with current sensor inputs. This approach allows the system to generate more precise and stable state estimates by leveraging stored contextual information. The proposed framework is rigorously evaluated through both extensive simulations and real-world experiments, demonstrating significant improvements in navigation accuracy and robustness compared to existing state-of-the-art visual-inertial solutions.

Elevated-order Fermi arcs, which are surface states of bulk higher-order topological insulators, can be extended into the bulk to form closed loops. Conversely, elevated-order Weyl points, which are topological singularities characteristic of standard Weyl semimetals, also admit extensions into various types of elevated configurations. This study introduces a novel class of square-root elevated-order Weyl semimetals, defined by elevated crystalline symmetries and specific boundary conditions. These conditions result in elevated topological invariants and the emergence of square-root elevated-order Weyl points, distinguished by singularities of elevated codimension and non-trivial monopole charges. These singularities manifest as elevated codimension trajectories in the momentum space band structure, with their positions determined by specific bulk real-space boundary conditions. The paper further examines the physical properties of these square-root elevated-order Weyl points, including their response to perturbations and the characteristics of surface and hinge states associated with them.

This study examines a data fulfillment problem for time-harmonic Maxwell's equations, where the objective is to determine an electric field that generates a magnetic field matching a specified target within a subdomain. We demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of solutions for this specific goal and subsequently develop a quasi-reversibility approach to approximate it. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to validate the method's efficacy.

Knowledge integration is a critical task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) that involves merging information from multiple sources to enhance model performance. However, existing methods face significant hurdles when dealing with private data, as they typically require centralized access, which is often unattainable in real-world scenarios. To address this, we introduce Federated Discriminative Aggregation (FedDA), a framework designed to facilitate knowledge integration across decentralized datasets. FedDA operates under strict privacy constraints, ensuring that data remains local while only sharing model parameters. To achieve effective aggregation, FedDA employs a two-stage strategy: it first estimates the data distribution shift among participating parties and subsequently uses these insights to dynamically adjust aggregation weights. We validate FedDA's efficacy through extensive experiments on text classification using three distinct NLP tasks across six datasets, demonstrating significant improvements over current state-of-the-art approaches.

This paper examines the rank development of elliptic curves within $S_4$ and $A_4$ quartic extensions of the rationals, specifically focusing on cases where the curve's rank increases by one in the base field. We establish a formula for the rank of the curve in the base field as a sum of local ranks across quadratic subfields, and we derive analogous results for the rank in the extension field.

The quantum null energy condition (QNEC) serves as a fundamental constraint on the expansion of entanglement, a principle that has been rigorously verified across a wide range of systems. This paper investigates the QNEC within the context of quantum thermodynamics, specifically examining the holographic expansion of entanglement in two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) at finite temperature. We introduce a novel framework for the thermodynamics of holographic disruptions and derive a general, model-independent upper limit for the entropy production resulting from such events. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this newly developed quantum thermodynamic approach accurately predicts the entropy generated by the holographic expansion of entanglement in both free and strongly coupled two-dimensional CFTs at finite temperature.

This study introduces a novel approach to quantify the velocity of a quantum state's evolution on the Bloch sphere by defining a state-dependent metric known as discriminability duration. This metric is derived from the Bures fidelity and is designed to quantify the distinguishability between a state and its infinitesimally displaced counterpart. We establish that this discriminability duration exhibits asymmetry monotonicity, a property that allows for the formulation of velocity limits for quantum evolution. Furthermore, we derive specific bounds for velocity within a two-level system evolving under a Hamiltonian with two parameters, analyzing how these limits vary as a function of that asymmetry.

This paper examines the interpolation operator $Q_n$ defined on the interval $[-1,1]$ using nodes consisting of the roots of the Chebyshev polynomial of degree $n+1$ and the endpoints $\pm 1$. For a specific class of functions $f$, we establish an estimate for the quantity $\sup_{x\in[-1,1]} \frac{\|Q_n(f)\|}{\|f\|}$, where $Q_n(g)$ denotes the unique polynomial of degree at most $n$ interpolating $g$ at the specified nodes.

Near-field scanning microwave microscopy (NSMM) is a technique that has been widely utilized to investigate the electromagnetic properties of materials and the structural integrity of devices. However, its application in the terahertz (THz) frequency range has been hindered by the lack of high-performance, low-loss THz tips and the inherent limitations of conventional near-field methods, which often fail to deliver sufficient spatial resolution for complex devices. This study introduces a novel approach to near-field THz imaging that utilizes a near-field optical microscope (NSOM) to map the near-field distribution of currents within coplanar resonators. By analyzing the far-field reflection spectra of these devices, researchers were able to identify the specific modes excited by the NSOM probe. Furthermore, the study demonstrates the use of near-field THz microscopy to visualize the near-field THz current distribution of a coplanar resonator, offering a pathway to explore the near-field THz characteristics of other devices.

This paper examines the long-term atmospheric evolution of Venus, with a specific focus on the mechanisms that regulate its climate. We begin by outlining the fundamental physical and chemical processes governing the atmosphere, followed by a detailed analysis of the feedback systems that maintain the current atmospheric state. Finally, we explore the potential drivers responsible for the planet's historical transformation from a likely Earth-like environment to its present-day conditions.

Multivariate point process models are frequently employed to analyze and forecast events within financial markets, social networks, and other domains. Among these, the multivariate Hawkes process stands out due to its ability to model mutual interactions between events. However, estimating its parameters is challenging, particularly when dealing with non-linearities. This paper introduces a Bayesian framework for estimating parameters in multivariate Hawkes processes that incorporate non-linear self-excitation. We evaluate the approach using both simulated data and real-world datasets, specifically examining high-frequency stock trades and cryptocurrency transactions. Furthermore, we apply the model to forecast the short-term volatility of Bitcoin.

We present a theoretical framework for analyzing the concurrent modification and amplification of linear polarization in ultra-intense laser pulses propagating through a magnetized plasma. This model integrates the paraxial approximation with a perturbative approach to solve Maxwell's equations, accounting for the influence of both the intense laser field and an external magnetic field on the plasma's dielectric properties. The study derives a set of coupled nonlinear partial differential equations governing the complex electric field envelope and polarization state. By solving these equations numerically, we demonstrate that a strong transverse magnetic field can significantly enhance the degree of linear polarization of a pulse that has already undergone initial modification. Furthermore, we investigate how varying the magnetic field's orientation relative to the laser's propagation direction affects this enhancement process.

We present a new measurement of the tau lepton's electric dipole moment (EDM) by analyzing data collected at the Belle II detector at the KEKB asymmetric-energy $e^+e^-$ collider. This analysis utilizes approximately 370 inverse femtobarns of data gathered during the initial phase of the Belle II operation. The study focuses on the radiative return process $e^+e^- \to \tau^+\tau^- \gamma$, where the photon is emitted from an initial-state electron or positron. The analysis strategy involves a broad kinematic scan of the photon energy spectrum to identify the most sensitive regions for detecting CP violation. The resulting constraint on the tau lepton EDM is $|d_\tau| < 1.1 \times 10^{-17} \, e\cdot\text{cm}$ at 90\% confidence level. This finding corresponds to an improvement of roughly a factor of two compared to the previous world limit.

This paper introduces a new decoding algorithm for rank-metric codes, specifically designed to handle symmetric measurement errors. This approach builds upon the well-known minimum distance decoder for rank-metric codes, which is typically restricted to asymmetric errors. The proposed method is applicable to a wide range of rank-metric codes, including Gabidulin codes, rank-metric Reed-Solomon codes, and rank-metric generalized Reed-Muller codes. The algorithm operates by decomposing a symmetric error into two components: an asymmetric error and a symmetric error of strictly lower rank. The decomposition ensures that the total Hamming weight of the resulting asymmetric error remains within the correction capability of the minimum distance decoder. The paper provides a formal proof of the algorithm's correctness and outlines its computational complexity. Finally, it presents simulation results demonstrating the algorithm's performance.

We examine the conformal block associated with a semi-infinite OPE segment in two-dimensional CFT$_2$, where one endpoint is anchored at a primary operator and the other extends to infinity. We demonstrate that the block for a primary operator located at the finite endpoint factorizes into the product of two bulk-to-boundary propagators within AdS$_2$, with the operator at the infinite end contributing a semi-infinite OPE segment block. We further establish a correspondence between the four-point function in two-dimensional CFT$_2$ and a two-point function involving semi-infinite OPE segments in AdS$_2$, which allows us to derive the former from the latter. Finally, we compute the block for a primary operator situated at the infinite end, showing that it factorizes into the product of two semi-infinite OPE segment blocks, each corresponding to a null line in AdS$_2$.

This note offers a new proof of Gelfand and MacPherson's enumerative formula for Pontrjagin classes, utilizing the method of localization on torus actions. The original derivation by Gelfand and MacPherson relied on enumerative geometry, whereas the authors have replaced that approach with torus action localization techniques.

We present new optical and near-infrared photometric data alongside new optical spectroscopy for SN 2020jfo, a Type II supernova characterized by a brief plateau in its light curve. This object was observed using the 2.3-meter Isaac Newton Telescope at La Palma, Spain, and the 1.5-meter T3 telescope at the Teide Observatory, Tenerife, Spain. The new spectra were obtained at the 2.3-meter William Herschel Telescope at La Palma, Spain. We also incorporate previously published data from the ZTF, ASAS-SN, and the Palomar Transient Factory to construct a comprehensive dataset. Our analysis indicates that SN 2020jfo is a Type II-P supernova with a plateau duration of approximately 90 days, peaking at an absolute magnitude of $M_V \approx -18.1$ mag. The new spectra reveal prominent features typical of Type II-P supernovae, including strong P Cygni profiles of H I, He I, and C II, alongside numerous absorption lines from intermediate-mass elements such as Ca II, Mg II, Si II, S II, and Fe II. This paper introduces a novel design for a lobster-eye X-ray telescope featuring a multiplexed lens array, engineered to deliver high-resolution imaging across a wide field of view. This configuration achieves its goals by integrating multiple distinct lens arrays, each optimized for a specific focal length, arranged so that their individual focal planes converge at a single common detector location. The resulting system functions as a multi-focal imaging setup, where each lens array covers a specific sub-region of the sky and projects its image onto a unique portion of the detector. This architecture enables the instrument to monitor a significantly broader field of view compared to traditional single-focal designs. Furthermore, the multiplexed approach offers inherent redundancy; if one lens array fails, the system can continue operating with reduced sensitivity in the corresponding field segment. This inherent fault tolerance makes the concept particularly well-suited for applications involving critical X-ray monitoring missions.

This work introduces a novel concept termed "stage set" uniform ellipticity, which serves as a stage-set adaptation of "partial uniform ellipticity." We establish that this new condition is equivalent to the standard formulation when the domain is a cube, and we examine its properties within the broader context of general domains. Furthermore, we apply this condition to analyze the boundary regularity of solutions to nonlinear elliptic equations.

The evolution of dark matter halos is governed by the interplay between gravitational forces and the stochastic nature of initial conditions. While the latter has been extensively investigated, the role of the cosmic velocity field remains less understood. This study employs deep learning to reconstruct the velocity field from the dark matter density field and analyzes its impact on halo mass assembly. Our results demonstrate that the velocity field significantly influences halo mass growth, with its effect intensifying as the universe evolves. Furthermore, we find that the velocity field correlates with halo mass, suggesting it serves as a valuable probe for dark matter halo mass estimation.

This study introduces a novel approach to modeling rotating stars within the framework of relativistic hydrodynamics, utilizing the 3+1 formalism and the Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) technique. This method allows for the simulation of stars rotating at various rates, including regimes approaching mass-shedding limits. The formulation is designed to be compatible with multiple equation-of-state types, accommodating both barotropic and baroclinic configurations. The current work focuses specifically on axisymmetric systems, where the governing equations are derived and solved using an iterative scheme. This strategy updates the metric and fluid variables iteratively until convergence is achieved, ensuring the new state satisfies all constraints, including hydrostatic equilibrium. The algorithm's validity is verified through comparisons with established results for both non-rotating and slowly rotating cases. Furthermore, the method is applied to investigate the structural properties of stars in rapid rotation, yielding new findings regarding the behavior of relativistic stars under extreme centrifugal forces.

Document extraction systems are increasingly utilized to automate the processing of unstructured text from sources like PDFs, images, and web pages. However, the advanced capabilities of these frameworks often come with a prohibitive cost, primarily driven by the need for extensive data labeling. To address this, we introduce a novel, cost-effective framework for creating high-quality labeled datasets specifically for document extraction. Our approach leverages a generative Large Language Model (LLM) to automatically generate JSON-structured labels for both images and PDFs. We validate our method using two distinct benchmarks: a custom dataset of 1,000 images and a dataset of 100,000 PDFs. Our results demonstrate that this framework successfully establishes a robust, affordable pipeline for constructing labeled datasets for document extraction tasks.

Gravitational waves (GWs) emitted by neutron star-black hole (NSBH) mergers offer a unique opportunity to investigate compact object physics and the dynamics of relativistic binary systems. However, accurately determining the nature of these events remains difficult because current theoretical models fail to produce distinctive electromagnetic signatures that can be easily identified. This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to automatically detect and classify NSBH merger gravitational waves. The methodology trains on a simulated dataset of both NSBH and binary neutron star (BNS) events, utilizing a convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify signals. The model successfully achieved a BNS identification accuracy of 99.99% and an NSBH classification accuracy of 99.98%. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that the deep learning approach can effectively isolate NSBH signals from BNS signals even when the input data contains significant noise.

Urban interactions are a primary driver of economic growth, yet the pandemic-induced shift toward remote activities has already begun to widen income-based disparities in urban mobility. This study investigates how behavioral changes during the pandemic intensified these gaps by analyzing urban mobility data from New York City. The research reveals that the decline in mobility for lower-income groups was significantly more severe than for higher-income groups, a phenomenon driven by the loss of in-person economic opportunities. Furthermore, the analysis indicates that the negative impact on mobility was not uniform; it disproportionately affected individuals with intermediate education levels and those working in the service sector. These findings suggest that the behavioral adaptations made necessary during the pandemic have exacerbated existing income-related inequalities in urban engagement.

The formation of massive stars remains a key unsolved problem in astrophysics, largely due to the difficulty in explaining how accretion proceeds rapidly enough to overcome radiation pressure limits. This study employs high-resolution, three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations to investigate episodic accretion and accretion disk evolution during the early stages of massive star formation. We find that gravitational instabilities trigger rapid disk growth, which facilitates the accumulation of mass through the formation of massive clumps. These clumps subsequently merge with the primary disk, enabling the central protostar to quickly reach high masses. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the episodic nature of accretion is driven by the episodic merging of these secondary disks. The resulting accretion rate variability is substantial, fluctuating by orders of magnitude over timescales ranging from hundreds to thousands of years. Finally, we show that the resulting accretion rate history and the associated episodicity are sensitive to the initial conditions of the protostellar system.

This work presents a Hamiltonian formulation for deep-water gravity waves characterized by uniform vorticity, utilizing a complex canonical variable defined by surface elevation and streamfunction. By applying a specific transformation to the canonical variables, the associated Dirac bracket is derived, which incorporates the effects of uniform vorticity. This framework enables the construction of a new Dysthe-type effective Hamiltonian that accounts for vorticity. The resulting Hamiltonian is validated through its ability to accurately model wave evolution across a spectrum of vorticity levels and steepnesses. Furthermore, the study investigates the impact of uniform vorticity on the stability of Stokes waves and the characteristics of wave breaking.

This paper introduces the concepts of differentiable maps and differential forms within the framework of locally arched spaces, which serve as a generalization of manifolds. It further establishes the Stokes theorem for these spaces and defines a specific category of such spaces that includes manifolds as a subcategory.

This study introduces a real-time navigation framework that merges a stratified controller with sonar data to enable autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to navigate complex environments. The proposed controller divides the control problem into two layers: a high-level planner generates a trajectory based on sonar inputs, while a low-level controller ensures precise tracking of that path. The high-level strategy employs a probabilistic approach to create a collision-free route, whereas the low-level system utilizes a sliding mode controller for robust trajectory adherence. Validation occurs in a simulated scenario featuring a cluttered underwater setting populated with various obstacles.

The proliferation of misinformation and false news on social media platforms poses a significant threat to public safety and security. This study introduces a novel approach to identifying fake news by leveraging text condensation, a technique that synthesizes multiple news articles into a concise summary. The core hypothesis is that authentic news stories exhibit greater semantic overlap compared to fabricated ones. Consequently, when genuine and fake reports are condensed, the resulting summaries of true news will demonstrate higher similarity to their source articles than the summaries derived from fake news. To validate this, we conducted experiments on the Twitter news dataset, which comprises real and fabricated stories sourced from Twitter. The findings indicate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in fake news detection.

This study examines the impact of surface curvature on the statistical properties of Gaussian stochastic fields defined over curved surfaces. We demonstrate that surface curvature modifies the field's covariance function, thereby influencing its spectral density. Specifically, we derive an exact expression for the spectral density on a sphere and provide approximate solutions for surfaces of revolution. Furthermore, we introduce a general perturbative approach to model spectral densities on arbitrary surfaces. Finally, we apply these findings to analyze the statistical characteristics of Gaussian fields on the sphere and within the Schwarzschild spacetime.

$\ell_1$-norm principal component (PC) analysis serves as a robust alternative to the standard $\ell_2$-norm approach, offering greater resilience against outliers. This study introduces a novel iterative algorithm designed to efficiently compute the $\ell_1$-norm PC and its associated variance for rotationally symmetric datasets. The proposed method guarantees convergence to the true $\ell_1$-norm PC and variance within a linear convergence rate. We validate the algorithm's efficacy and performance through both synthetic experiments and real-world data applications.

Emotion-related inquiries, such as "Why did the movie make you cry?", are notoriously difficult for question-answering systems to handle effectively. Addressing this challenge, we introduce a novel method that leverages BERT-based semantic tagging to identify and tag the emotional components within these questions. Our approach utilizes a tagger to detect the specific elements driving the emotion and employs a question generator to construct a semantically equivalent, answerable variant of the original query. We evaluated our framework on the EmQuAC dataset, demonstrating that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we conducted an in-depth analysis of the generated answers and the system's performance to provide further insights.

Navigating unfamiliar environments effectively requires both an understanding of the surroundings and the ability to recall past experiences. To address this, we introduce HiTMap, a hierarchical topological diagram representation designed to depict these new settings. Our approach involves learning to generate these maps through the use of a hierarchical latent variable model applied to visual data. Specifically, we decompose the mapping process into two stages: first, identifying a coarse layout of the environment, and subsequently, localizing the agent within that established structure. We validate our method through experiments in both simulated and real-world settings, demonstrating its efficacy in generating accurate representations of previously unexplored areas.

Atomic interferometry is emerging as a highly sensitive technique for detecting local magnetic field variations, offering a promising route to non-invasive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This study introduces a novel approach to observe the Meissner effect of a superconductor using atomic interferometry. By analyzing the resulting interferometric phase shifts, we demonstrate that the magnetic field distribution generated by the Meissner effect can be reconstructed with high sensitivity. Furthermore, we show that this method enables the detection of minute magnetic field changes in the vicinity of a superconductor.

This paper introduces a novel geometric framework for analyzing finite mixture models, establishing a direct link to stochastic geometry and Choquet theory. Within this setting, a finite mixture model is defined as a stochastic process where the mixing distribution is selected from a finite set of probability measures. We demonstrate that the distribution function of such a process corresponds to a simplex-valued, multivariate polynomial of degree $n$, where $n$ represents the cardinality of the mixing set. Furthermore, we define a canonical representation for these models and prove that the model's parameters are uniquely determined if and only if the underlying mixing set is in general position.

GPGPU technology has become a standard for executing computationally demanding tasks, yet its memory architecture remains constrained by a lack of concurrency, which hampers performance in object-oriented programming. Existing GPU memory allocators typically rely on a single, global free list managed by a central allocator, causing threads to contend for memory and suffer from serialization. This paper introduces DynaSOAr, a novel GPU memory allocator designed to eliminate this contention by maintaining separate free lists within each thread block. By utilizing a block-local allocator, DynaSOAr enables threads to access memory concurrently and efficiently. Furthermore, it optimizes memory access patterns to enhance performance. Evaluation results indicate that DynaSOAr achieves a 1.5x to 2.5x speedup compared to current allocators when executing object-oriented benchmarks.

This study employs a relative initial principles approach to investigate the structural and electronic characteristics of Mn adatoms and dimers situated on a Nb(110) surface. To achieve this, the research utilizes the GGA+U method within the VASP framework. The findings reveal that the most stable configuration for the Mn adatom is a single atom adsorbed atop the Nb(110) plane, with a calculated adsorption energy of 3.0 eV. In contrast, the preferred arrangement for Mn dimers involves two atoms forming a linear chain oriented parallel to the Nb(110) surface, exhibiting a binding energy of 1.1 eV. Furthermore, the research analyzes the magnetic properties of these systems, noting that the adatom possesses a magnetic moment of 3.0 $\mu_{\text{B}}$, while the dimer exhibits a reduced moment of 1.8 $\mu_{\text{B}}$. Finally, the research examines the density of states and the projected orbital density of states to elucidate the bonding mechanisms and the origin of the observed magnetism.

Located 100 pc away, the TOI-712 system hosts three planets with radii ranging from 1.8 to 2.4 Earth radii and orbital periods between 10 and 20 days. We have determined the system's masses and densities using radial velocity measurements obtained from the HARPS and CARMENES spectrographs. The resulting densities, which span 1.8 to 3.5 g cm$^{-3}$, indicate that the planets consist of significant hydrogen/helium envelopes atop rocky cores. The innermost planet, TOI-712 b, is identified as a mini-Neptune with a radius of 1.8 R$_{\oplus}$ and a mass of 5.5 M$_{\oplus}$, orbiting at 0.07 AU with an eccentricity of 0.003 $\pm$ 0.002. Its estimated equilibrium temperature of 600 K suggests it resides in the inner edge of the habitable zone, yet its youth—approximately 100 million years—likely prevents the formation of a stable atmosphere. The outer planets, TOI-712 c and d, are classified as sub-Neptunes with masses of 10.1 and 12.1 M$_{\oplus}$, respectively, and radii of 2.2 and 2.4 R$_{\oplus

Utilizing hybrid DFT calculations, this study examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of carbon- and nitrogen-infused rutile TiO$_2$ (100) surfaces. By employing a supercell model, individual and co-substituted configurations for C and N dopants were analyzed. The findings indicate that both dopants preferentially occupy interstitial sites within the TiO$_2$ lattice. Furthermore, the results reveal that the magnetic state of the system is highly sensitive to dopant concentration and specific doping arrangements.

The recent discovery of the Higgs boson at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has established the Standard Model (SM) as a complete theory of electroweak symmetry breaking. However, the origin of the mass hierarchy remains unresolved, with the most prevalent hypothesis suggesting that new physics emerges near the electroweak scale. This scenario implies the existence of new degrees of freedom that interact with the Higgs boson, potentially leading to the production of top quark pairs in an elastic state. Such a phenomenon would manifest as a distinct signature in the $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass spectrum at the LHC. This paper offers a comprehensive review of the theoretical framework describing elastic top quark production, including the necessary experimental analysis techniques. Furthermore, it examines the implications of this hypothesis for the search of new physics at the LHC.

Let $G$ be an infinite graph with components $C_1, C_2, \dots$. We establish that for any positive integer $k$, there exists an integer $N$ such that if the vertex set of $G$ is partitioned into $k$ color classes, at least one monochromatic component $C_i$ contains a subgraph $H$ where the edges of $H$ are colored with a single color $c \in \{1, \dots, k\}$ and the minimum degree of $H$ satisfies $\delta(H) \geq N$. This result generalizes a theorem by Erd\H{o}s and Seidenberg (1943), which addressed the case $k=2$. We also examine the scenario where $G$ is a tree, providing a characterization of the minimum degree required for a monochromatic component to contain a monochromatic copy of a given tree $T$.

This study examines the simulation of scalar quantum electrodynamics (sQED) using a quantum computer simulation with qutrits. We analyze the system's behavior across various ultraviolet cutoffs and initial particle densities, specifically investigating how the vacuum instability and subsequent particle production are influenced by these parameters. Our findings indicate that the critical density for instability is lower when modeled with qutrits compared to standard qubit-based simulations. Furthermore, we observe that the resulting particle densities and energy levels surpass the critical threshold, causing the system to enter a highly excited state. This state is characterized by a significant enhancement in the sound speed relative to its initial value.

We present experimental findings regarding positron production using laser-illuminated foil targets within the QED-dominated regime. The data reveal a distinct positron energy spectrum characterized by a sharp cutoff and a pronounced polarization effect, with spins oriented perpendicular to the reaction plane. This polarization reaches a maximum of approximately 80% at the highest energy threshold. The observed phenomena are consistent with theoretical predictions derived from a QED-based Monte Carlo simulation.

A group $G$ is classified as limited if there exists a constant $c$ such that for any finite subset $A \subseteq G$ with cardinality $|A| \geq c$, the growth of the set $A^2$ satisfies $|A^2| \leq |A|$. This paper demonstrates that any group $G$ featuring a non-trivial abelian limited subgroup $H$ with polynomial growth exponent $d$ must possess polynomial group growth. Furthermore, it is shown that any group $G$ containing a non-trivial solvable limited subgroup $H$ with polynomial growth exponent $d$ exhibits polynomial group growth of degree at most $d^{|H|}$. Finally, the authors establish that any group $G$ containing a non-trivial nilpotent limited subgroup $H$ with polynomial growth exponent $d$ also demonstrates polynomial group growth, bounded by degree $d^{d^{|H|}}$.

This paper introduces the concept of geometric configurations within Lie groupoids, which serve as a generalization of both smooth stacks and Lie algebroids. The authors establish a comprehensive theory of these configurations, demonstrating that every smooth stack can be expressed as a geometric configuration in a canonical manner. Furthermore, they define a universal Lie groupoid associated with any given configuration and prove that this structure is unique up to equivalence. The work culminates in a characterization of geometric configurations as a monadic functor over the category of Lie groupoids.

The formation of the most massive stars remains a subject of debate, with theories divided between models requiring rapid accretion despite strong stellar feedback and those relying on the suppression of star formation by that same feedback. A primary unresolved issue is how gas concentrates within dense, dark molecular clouds to reach the high densities required for these massive stars to ignite. This study presents new, high-resolution ALMA observations of the Dragon Infrared Dark Nebula (IRDC), a prominent star-forming region located in the Galactic plane. These images reveal a dense, elongated filamentary structure containing a prominent, massive protostar embedded within a compact, bright clump. The data indicate that the core is currently expanding, a phenomenon likely triggered by the feedback from the newborn star. This expansion drives a bow shock into the surrounding envelope, creating a distinct, expanding cavity. The findings suggest that core expansion serves as a critical mechanism for concentrating gas and facilitating the formation of massive stars.

This work introduces the concept of one-step relations for stationary stochastic fields defined on the sphere, extending the well-known framework of one-step linear prediction from Euclidean space. We establish that the sphere admits a unique, most parsimonious representation of these fields via a one-step relation, provided the field is not purely deterministic. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the associated coefficients function as a spherical analog to the spectral factorization of the field's spectral density. Finally, we examine the asymptotic behavior of these coefficients as the field's resolution increases.

The mechanical behavior of liquid foams is governed by the interplay between surface tension and the roughness of their Plateau borders. This study introduces a novel scaling framework to characterize the resistance of these structures to shear flow. By integrating the classic Plateau-LeChatelier effect with a new model for surface tension variations caused by wall roughness, the authors derive a relationship that connects the yield stress to the specific geometry of the walls. This work offers a fresh perspective on the rheology of liquid foams, with potential applications in industrial processing and the study of geological fault mechanics.

Skin cancer represents a significant global health challenge, with melanoma being the most lethal form. Early detection is critical for effective treatment, yet it remains difficult for medical professionals to identify in its initial stages. Consequently, there is an urgent need for automated systems capable of diagnosing skin lesions. This study introduces a novel outlier detection framework designed to identify skin cancer, leveraging deep learning techniques. The proposed method utilizes a ResNet-50 architecture trained on a dataset of 10,000 images, incorporating a disorder metric to flag cancerous samples as anomalies. By treating cancer as an outlier, the model achieves a 99.99% accuracy on a private test set, demonstrating that this approach offers a highly effective solution for skin cancer diagnosis.

This study examines the fingering instability within a spinning Hele-Shaw cell, where a fluid is injected between two parallel plates. We analyze how rotation influences the formation of fluid fingers, demonstrating that a critical spin rate exists beyond which fingers cannot develop. We further explore the impact of varying spin rates on finger characteristics, including their width, length, and count. Our findings reveal that finger width decreases as spin increases, whereas finger length and total number increase with higher rotation speeds. Finally, we present a theoretical model to explain the observed fingering behavior.

The detection of ethynyl cyclopentadiene (C$_5$H$_4$C$_2$H) in TMC-1 was first reported in 2013, yet its identification remained uncertain due to the lack of a definitive laboratory spectrum. This ambiguity persisted until 2018, when the discovery of a CN-substituted isomer in TMC-1 provided the necessary spectral data to confirm the original finding. In this study, we present the first-ever laboratory spectrum of the CN-substituted isomer, which we identify as 1-cyano-1,3-cyclopentadiene. We achieved this by synthesizing the molecule and recording its spectrum using a pulsed discharge Fourier transform microwave spectrometer. The observed transitions were analyzed within the framework of the effective Hamiltonian method, allowing us to determine rotational and centrifugal distortion constants for both ground and excited torsional states. These parameters were subsequently employed to simulate the spectrum of the CCH-substituted isomer, 1-ethynyl-1,3-cyclopentadiene, thereby confirming the identification made by the initial TMC-1 discovery team.
